selection_rationale: Neutrik connectors are the de-facto reference in European stage, studio and broadcast rigs and Neutrik publishes full per-part data sheets, so the connector families (XLR3/XLR5, TRS/TS, speakON NL4/NL8, powerCON TRUE1, etherCON, opticalCON, 75 ohm BNC) are taken from Neutrik, with HARTING Han for multipins. Cables come from Sommer cable (German, widely sold in France), Canare and Mogami, picking one clear reference per sub_type (twisted-pair and star-quad mic, 2.5 mm² speaker, 8-pair multicore, 110 ohm AES and 75 ohm coax, Cat.7 PUR, OS2 fibre, DB25 fan-out). Discontinued candidates (NL4FX, NE8MC, NAC3FX-W-TOP) were replaced by their Neutrik-named successors; Belden, Switchcraft and LEMO sites blocked fetches.

devices.model: NC3MXX (XLR 3-pole male cable connector, XX series)
devices.technology: XLR male 3-pole cable connector with solder contacts and latch lock, compliant with IEC 61076-2-103 (per Neutrik).
devices.why_it_is_a_classic: The XX series is Neutrik's general-purpose XLR cable connector, the plug found on most mic and line leads. The 3-pole XLR is the standard balanced mic/line connector (pin 1 shield, pin 2 hot, pin 3 cold per EIA RS-297-A as reported by Wikipedia).

key_specs.pin_assignment_balanced_audio: Pin 1: chassis ground (cable shield); pin 2: positive polarity (hot); pin 3: negative polarity (cold) (EIA RS-297-A, as reported by Wikipedia)
key_specs.phantom_power: Pins 2 and 3 both carry +48 V ±4 V DC relative to pin 1 (DPA, citing IEC 61938:2018)

manuals.title: Assembly instruction NC*FXX & NC*MXX XLR cable connector (BDA 158)

devices.notes: Pin assignment comes from Wikipedia, which cites EIA RS-297-A; the AES14 and IEC 60268-12 texts could not be reached (aes.org returned 403). Wikipedia also notes that some older US equipment used pin 3 hot. Neutrik's pages give no introduction year.

tekpractice.sim_value_reason: The basic XLR3 connector: gender, pin 2 hot, and phantom on pins 2/3 are core wiring lessons.

devices.technology: speakON 4-pole female cable connector with twist lock and screw terminals (per Neutrik).
devices.why_it_is_a_classic: speakON is Neutrik's loudspeaker connector family; NL4FXX-W-S is the listed successor of the discontinued NL4FX, the long-standing 4-pole speaker cable plug.

key_specs.warning: Not intended for use as an AC mains or power supply connector; not for interrupting current (per Neutrik)

devices.notes: The older NL4FX (40 A rms continuous, Quick Lock latch, cable OD 7–14.5 mm) is marked discontinued on neutrik.com, which lists NL4FXX-W-S (6–12 mm) and NL4FXX-W-L (10–16 mm) as successors. No pin assignment (1+/1-/2+/2-) was found on the pages read.

devices.technology: speakON 8-pole female cable connector, Quick Lock latch, screw terminals (per Neutrik).
devices.why_it_is_a_classic: The 8-pole speakON carries up to four 2-wire speaker circuits in one connector, used for multi-way amplifier links.

key_specs.rated_current: 30 A rms continuous per contact; 40 A audio signal at 50% duty cycle
key_specs.warning: speakON is NOT to be used as an AC mains or power supply connector (per Neutrik)

devices.notes: Status set to 'not found' because the product page states no lifecycle status and lists no successor. 'speakon-nl8' is a proposed connector id.

tekpractice.sim_value_reason: Multi-way amp links; teaches that one 8-pole cable carries 4 speaker circuits.

devices.technology: powerCON TRUE1 lockable single-phase mains cable connector (2 + PE) with twist lock and circuit breaking capability (per Neutrik).
devices.why_it_is_a_classic: powerCON TRUE1 is Neutrik's lockable mains connector that can be connected or disconnected under load; it is the listed successor of the phased-out NAC3FX-W-TOP (TRUE1 TOP) cable connector.

key_specs.breaking_capacity: Yes (CBC), can be connected or disconnected under load or live
key_specs.protection_class: IP65 / IP67 (mated or with closed caps)

devices.notes: The requested candidate NAC3FX-W-TOP (powerCON TRUE1 TOP) is marked phased out on neutrik.com with NAC3F-TRUE1-S named as replacement (TOP version: 16 A EU / 20 A US, 250 V AC, IP65 only with SCNAC-FX cover). Status of NAC3F-TRUE1-S is not stated on its page.

tekpractice.sim_value_reason: Mains link on powered speakers; breaking capacity vs classic blue/grey powerCON.

devices.technology: etherCON male cable connector carrier that locks a user-supplied pre-assembled RJ45 plug (per Neutrik).
devices.why_it_is_a_classic: etherCON adds a robust XLR-style locking shell to RJ45 for stage networks (Dante, AES50, etc.); NE8MX is the named successor of the discontinued NE8MC.

key_specs.compatibility_note: Does not mate with CAT6 chassis connectors NE8FDY-C6 / NE8FDY-C6-B (per Neutrik)

tekpractice.sim_value_reason: etherCON vs plain RJ45 and the Cat6 chassis non-intermating trap.

devices.technology: Rugged fibre-optic chassis connector with LC-Duplex feedthrough and 4 solder contacts, push-pull locking (per Neutrik).
devices.why_it_is_a_classic: opticalCON is Neutrik's ruggedised fibre connector family for stage and broadcast; the DUO version wraps a standard LC-Duplex link in a locking metal housing.

devices.model: NBNC75BLP7 (rearTWIST HD BNC 75 Ω cable connector)

key_specs.vswr_return_loss: ≤1.050/>32 dB up to 1 GHz; ≤1.065/>30 dB up to 2 GHz; ≤1.100/>26 dB up to 3 GHz
key_specs.suitable_cables: Belden 8241, Canare LV-61S, CommScope 5563, RG59B/U and others
key_specs.termination: crimp (pin 1.6 mm square, shield 6.47 mm hex, IEC 60803)

devices.model: Gold DB25-XLRM (8-channel analog DB25 to XLR male fan-out)
devices.technology: 8-channel analog fan-out: DB25 D-sub to 8 gold-pin XLR male, metal D-sub shell with thumb screws (per Mogami).
devices.why_it_is_a_classic: DB25 fan-outs are the standard way to connect 8-channel DB25 interfaces (Avid, converters, patchbays) to XLR gear; Mogami's Gold version is wired with the 'industry standard analog pin-out'.
typical_uses: interface DB25 outputs to XLR inputs

key_specs.channels: Eight channels, analog in or out
key_specs.connectors: DB25 to gold pin XLR male
key_specs.pinout: industry standard analog pin-out (standard not named by Mogami)
key_specs.shell: all metal D-sub shells with metal thumb screws

devices.notes: Mogami does not name the pinout standard; the catalogue distinguishes 'Tascam' and 'Yamaha' AES formats only for its digital DB25 cables. The XLR male end makes this an output-side loom (DB25 out to XLR inputs). Analog vs AES (digital) DB25 looms are not interchangeable.

tekpractice.sim_value_reason: Already in catalog; DB25 pinout and channel-to-XLR mapping lesson.
